prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural-language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject, visible actions and object interactions, and the setting. Use specific action verbs and name any clear maneuvers; indicate direction of movement (toward/away/from the camera, left/right, up/down) and whether motions are simultaneous, and state if a person or object is mid‑air or contacting the ground. Describe body posture with concrete terms (standing, kneeling, squatting, crouching, seated upright, reclining, leaning forward/back, perched) rather than interpretive labels, and report facial expressions or gaze only when they are visually evident (e.g., smiling; eyes looking toward X). Give precise spatial relationships and scale (next to, behind, in front of, atop, a few feet/meters apart) and note the number or flow of people (isolated, a small group, a line, a crowd). Describe lighting, shadows, and visible surface textures or effects using observable cues (directional backlight, side light, diffuse/overcast light, strong cast shadows and their direction/length; wet pavement, puddles, splashes, reflections, motion blur) when present. Avoid speculation or subjective judgments; state intentions or purposes only when directly supported by visible evidence (e.g., “reaching toward” or “placing on a table”). Keep the caption concrete, image-centered, and limited to one clear sentence.
